candidates.label: Sea of Adria (label point, between Italy and Greece)
candidates.support: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia traces how the name "Adria," first applied only to the sea's northern end near the Italian town of Atria, had by the first century been extended southward until it could cover "even the waters between Crete and Malta"; the encyclopedia cites the first-century Jewish historian Josephus's own account of being shipwrecked "in the middle of the Adria" on a voyage from Cyrene toward Puteoli, a central Mediterranean crossing. OpenBible.info's point for this broader first-century sense, covering both today's Adriatic and Ionian Seas, matches Wikidata's point for the Ionian Sea exactly.

summary.text: The Sea of Adria is the body of water where Acts places Paul's ship as it was "driven back and forth" for fourteen days after a storm, before it neared the shore of Malta. The name, drawn from the Italian town of Atria near the mouth of the Po, first named only the sea's northern reach, but ancient writers had extended it by the first century to also cover the Ionian Sea and, in some authors, the waters between Crete and Malta, which fits the ship's actual course.

history.text: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia documents the name's gradual spread in ancient usage: first confined to the sea near Atria, it grew to reach the Abruzzi and the Strait of Otranto, and in some ancient authors even to the Gulf of Taranto, the sea off Sicily, and the waters between Crete and Malta; the encyclopedia cites the sixth-century Byzantine historian Procopius placing Malta itself at the Adria's western edge.

The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia compares Acts' account to the first-century Jewish historian Josephus's own report, in his autobiography, of being shipwrecked "in the middle of the Adria" while sailing from Cyrene toward Puteoli, and of being picked up by a ship headed the same way; the encyclopedia treats this as evidence for the same broad, first-century sense of "Adria" that Acts uses.

scripture.textWEB: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

politicalHistory.entity: Open sea between Roman Italy, Macedonia/Achaia, and the island of Crete; this feature has no single political area of its own on this map
